acceptance: Rendering from explicit values (token substitution of [NAME.k] and [NAME]) produces the expected qualification SQL for Q39, Q44, Q93 and Q8 (400-zip list), and rendering a template from its own -LOG values reproduces dsqgen's SQL for all 99 queries
generate_with_parameters is deleted or replaced by a working implementation with tests
Findings and limits are recorded in this item
context:
Source: DataFrame query parity proposal v3 (item T16). Owner decision D3 is in dfparity-t00-owner-decisions. Do not adopt the tpcds_obt/query_conversion.py renderer (it collapses random() to its lower bound and dist to 0). Project owner does NOT accept earlier reviewers' TPC-H claims.

Progress 2026-10-01: implemented and published as PR #2510 (branch feat/tpcds-render-with-parameters, worktree ../BenchBox.wt-tpcds-render-params, head 2089a0c84), held, auto-merge withheld; make pr-preflight exit 0 on that head (a first run failed the windows-antipatterns guard on a read_text() without encoding, fixed). FINDINGS (TESTED): (1) Constant-define rendering alone (define NAME=value;) round-trips to identical SQL for 70 of 99 templates (seed 7 render, -LOG values, re-render with seed 99); the other 29 use multi-value defines (ZIP list, CATEGORY.1-3, STATE.1-3, COLOR, ...). (2) Token substitution of [NAME.k] and [NAME] (for k=1) in the staged template, with no define rewriting, round-trips to identical SQL for 99 of 99, including Q8's 400-zip ulist and Q89 (whose CLASS_* defines depend on [IDX.k]). Implemented that as DSQGenBinary.generate_with_parameters (values keyed by -LOG names such as YEAR.01; unknown or malformed names raise ValueError; returns the same SQL as generate()). (3) Qualification-style values verified for Q39 (YEAR.01=2001, MONTH.01=1), Q44 (STORE.01=4, NULLCOLSS.01=ss_addr_sk) and Q93 (REASON.01=reason 28), independent of the seed; Q8 with 400 zips works. (4) LIMIT: -LOG still reports dsqgen's own random draws, not the injected values, because the defines stay in place, so this item's acceptance wording 'and -LOG echoes the injected values' is NOT met by this approach; the SQL carries the values. Constant defines would echo them for scalars but cannot express list values. (5) The old stub is replaced and its no-op test removed. Not done: committing the qualification values (dfparity-t17), a whole-set 99-template round-trip test (needs the parser from PR #2498; currently a script result and 6 pinned templates). Remaining: hosted CI, maintainer merge, then finish.
description: DSQGenBinary.generate_with_parameters (benchbox/core/tpcds/c_tools.py:890-921) is a no-op: it renders with dsqgen first, then replaces [NAME] tokens that no longer exist. dsqgen -QUALIFY does not change values (tested). The spec lists qualification values in the same NAME.NN = value vocabulary that -LOG writes (verified in the spec text: MANUFACT.01 = 738, REASON.01 = reason 28, matching the DataFrame defaults for Q41 and Q93). A prior reviewer rendered qualification SQL by staging templates with constant defines (define YEAR=2001;) for Q39, Q44 and Q93 and saw -LOG echo the values; I did not re-run that. Spike the approach, including Q8's 400-zip ulist, then delete or replace the stub.
